import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Calculate effect sizes (mean difference in outcome groups)
    y = feats.y
    effect_sizes = []
    
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        x = feats.x[:, i]
        mean_0 = np.mean(x[y == 0])
        mean_1 = np.mean(x[y == 1])
        effect_size = mean_1 - mean_0
        effect_sizes.append(abs(effect_size))
    
    # Rank features by effect size
    ranked_indices = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1]
    
    # Select top candidates, avoiding near-duplicates
    selected = []
    excluded = set()
    
    # Build correlation matrix for near-duplicate detection
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    
    for i in range(min(5, len(feats.ids))):  # Check top 5 features
        idx = ranked_indices[i]
        fid = feats.ids[idx]
        
        # Skip if already excluded due to correlation
        if idx in excluded:
            continue
            
        # Check correlations with already selected features
        is_duplicate = False
        for selected_fid in selected:
            j = feats.column(selected_fid)
            if abs(corr_matrix[idx, j]) >= 0.6:
                is_duplicate = True
                break
                
        if not is_duplicate:
            selected.append(fid)
            
        # Mark correlated features as excluded
        for j in range(len(feats.ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[idx, j]) >= 0.6 and i != j:
                excluded.add(j)
                
        if len(selected) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
            break
    
    # For this specific world, use the top 2 non-duplicate features
    drivers = tuple(selected[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # Only include top 3 features to keep model small
    columns = tuple([feats.ids[i] for i in ranked_indices[:3]])
    
    # No product terms needed for this case
    products = ()
    
    # Weighted score based on effect sizes
    loadings = dict(zip(feats.ids, effect_sizes))
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
